verified.subsystem: Vault reward accrual & Convex claim manager
verified.exploit: With forceClaimAfter>0 the Convex CRV/CVX index is frozen mid-window while rewards keep accruing in Convex; an attacker deposits a large collateral position just before the window expires (their mint's _claimVaultRewards no-ops, so their debt is pinned at the stale pre-jump index), waits for expiry, calls claimRewardTokens() to trigger the lump claim which _accumulateSecondaryRewardViaClaim splits across current (post-deposit) shares, then claims via lendingRouter.claimRewards — capturing a per-share slice of a whole window's rewards for only a few blocks of holding and diluting time-weighted honest holders.
verified.poc_sketch: Extend TestRewardManager harness: migrateRewardPool with forceClaimAfter=7 days; honest user enterPosition(defaultDeposit) and hold; warp ~7 days and MockRewardPool.setRewardAmount=windowReward (simulating a full window of Convex accrual); just before expiry attacker enterPosition with a large deposit and assert the vault index is unchanged and getRewardDebt(attacker)==attackerSharesindex_old/1e18; warp past expiry; call claimRewardTokens() then lendingRouter.claimRewards(vault) as attacker and assert attackerReward ≈ windowRewardattackerShares/effectiveSupply_after (a full-window slice) despite ~0 holding time, while the honest holder's claim is diluted well below the no-attacker baseline, and net attacker gain exceeds LP entry/exit slippage.
verified.reason: The forceClaimAfter>0 early-return freezes accumulatedRewardPerVaultShare across the window so a just-in-time depositor's rewardDebt is pinned at the stale index, while the later lump claim divides a whole window's Convex rewards by the current post-deposit effectiveSupply, letting the unprivileged attacker claim a proportional slice with no deposit-time settlement or minimum-holding guard.
